content.comment_body: Hello, I am experiencing an issue with [product_name] expansion modules. The system includes a [product_name] [article_no] together with four [product_name] [article_no] digital modules and one [product_name] [article_no] analog module. This setup operated reliably for several years, but recently all the expansion modules began to intermittently switch their LED indicators from green to orange, eventually remaining orange in the initialization state. Troubleshooting steps I took include: - Disconnecting all wires except the power supply from the modules to rule out EMC interference - Changing the power supply from 24VAC to a 24VDC unit by [company_name]; the AC supply measured 27.4VAC output, while the manual lists a maximum of 26.4VAC - Removing and redownloading the program, which contains approximately 100 blocks - Replacing all hardware (expansion modules and switching the base module to a different version) None of these actions resolved the problem. I still suspect EMC issues, since two 75kW softstarters are installed in the same cabinet and their power rails are only about 30cm away from the [product_name] hardware, which shares this rail for its power supply. Measurements of the [product_name] power input using an oscilloscope showed a clean sine wave without peaks or distortion. Each output is connected via a coupling relay. Thanks in advance for any suggestions. Best regards [user_name]

It could be that the contacts of the expansion module connecting slides are contaminated; I've encountered this before. Try cleaning the connecting slides with contact spray and moving them back and forth to improve the connection, and make sure all procedures are done with the system powered off.
Hello [user_name], Thank you for your suggestion. I will attempt to clean and treat the connecting slide contacts with contact spray to see if it resolves the issue. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The core issue discussed involves expansion modules for a [product_name] controller unexpectedly switching their LEDs from green to orange—indicating initialization errors. Despite trying various fixes such as rewiring, upgrading the power supply, reloading software, and hardware replacement, the fault persists. One user raised the possibility of dirty contacts on the connecting slides between modules, suggesting that reliability may depend on routine maintenance in addition to electrical or software troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] system and its expansion modules to be robust and stable when used in industrial settings, and for the modules to avoid or quickly recover from unexpected initialization problems.
